qt: to the Commission Anthony Smith (The Left) Subject:

In a European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights survey, 57 % of intersex persons who had undergone surgery or hormonal treatment said that neither they nor their parents had given fully informed consent. On 27 October 2026, the European Commission against Racism and Intolerance noted that unnecessary interventions of that type were not explicitly banned in Belgium. The treatments, which were sometimes carried out repeatedly since childhood, could entail irreversible side effects: chronic pain, loss of sensation, infertility and long-term psychological trauma. In October 2025, the Council of Europe recommended that procedures that could be postponed should be deferred until personal consent could be obtained, with strict exceptions. In April 2026, the Economic, Social and Environmental Council called for binding safeguards. However, the 2026-2030 LGBTIQ+ Strategy does not set out any specific measures or time lines. The recommendation on harmful practices announced in 2020 has not yet been published. 1.

Beyond best practices, what real measures does the Commission intend to present – and following what time line – in order to prevent interventions that are not medically necessary and to postpone any acts that can be until the child can give his or her free and informed consent, irrespective of parental consent?
Will it review binding instruments falling under EU competences and publish a monitoring of effective protection and remedies available in the Member States as early as the 2028 stocktaking exercise?
Does it intend to make EU funding conditional on compliance with these guarantees and support real access to medical records, redress and compensation for the damage suffered?
